items.text: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
items.hook: Don’t outsource wisdom to your gut alone.
items.lesson: First-principles thinking still needs humility. Lean on understanding — but don’t make it the only pillar.

items.text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
items.lesson: Sharp work usually comes from friction with people who care.

items.text: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
items.lesson: Before you ship a big bet, widen the circle.

items.text: He who gives answer before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
items.lesson: Hear the full problem before you propose the fix.

items.text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
items.lesson: Solo decision-making at scale is a shared failure mode for nations and startups.

items.text: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
items.lesson: Agency and contingency coexist — adapt when reality redirects the path.

items.text: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.
items.lesson: Budget time and money for real learning, not just content.

items.text: A prudent man sees danger, and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
items.lesson: Seeing danger and stepping aside isn’t fear — it’s compounding survival.

items.text: That which has been is that which shall be; and that which has been done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
items.hook: History rhymes — product cycles do too.
items.lesson: When a “new” pattern feels unprecedented, check the archive.

items.text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
items.hook: Timing is a strategy, not just luck.
items.lesson: Ask if this is a plant season or a prune season.

items.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
items.hook: Three verbs beat a thousand slogans.
items.lesson: Justice, mercy, humility — a compact ethics checklist for power.

items.text: But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
items.lesson: Ask whether fairness is episodic — or flowing.

items.text: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”
items.hook: Stillness is a skill under noise.
items.lesson: Doomscrolling thrives on urgency. Stillness creates judgment.

items.text: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
items.hook: Scarcity of time is the real budget.
items.lesson: Wisdom starts when you admit the calendar is finite.

items.text: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Judge the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
items.lesson: Pair study with concrete defense of someone else.

items.text: Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
items.hook: The golden rule is a product principle.
items.lesson: Treat the other side as you’d want to be treated under the same constraints.

items.text: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
items.hook: Debug yourself before you debug the team.
items.lesson: Clear your own beam so feedback becomes useful, not theater.

items.text: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
items.lesson: Prefer costly truth over cheap narrative — in news, markets, and self-talk.

items.text: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
items.lesson: Renewing the mind is deliberate rewiring against feed algorithms and stale defaults.

items.text: Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever things are honorable, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think about these things.
items.lesson: Curate inputs the way you’d curate training data.

items.text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
items.hook: Listen first. Speak second. Anger last.
items.lesson: A three-step latency budget for hard conversations and headlines.

items.text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
items.lesson: Close the loop: one action from what you just learned.

items.text: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
items.lesson: Precise language is how builders turn fog into work.

items.text: Moreover you shall provide out of all the people able men which fear God: men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
items.lesson: Hire for character, then cascade authority.

items.text: Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.
items.hook: Commit the work — then release the outcome.
items.lesson: Planning is yours; results aren’t a control panel.

items.text: Know well the state of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds:
items.hook: Know the state of your flocks.
items.lesson: Dashboards beat vibes — inspect what you own before it drifts.

items.text: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
items.hook: Whatever your hand finds — do it with might.
items.lesson: Half-effort compounds into mediocrity. Finish the pass.

items.text: But those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
items.hook: Strength renews when you stop forcing the sprint.
items.lesson: Burnout is often a pacing error. Wait, then run.

items.text: Don’t rejoice against me, my enemy. When I fall, I will arise. When I sit in darkness, Yahweh will be a light to me.
items.lesson: Recovery is part of the strategy — expect setbacks, plan the rise.

items.text: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
items.lesson: Clarity beats clever hedges in product, politics, and promises.

items.text: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
items.hook: Tomorrow’s anxiety is a tax on today.
items.lesson: Worry borrows trouble you can’t spend yet. Act on what’s in range.

items.text: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
items.lesson: How you handle pennies predicts how you’ll handle platforms.

items.text: Let us not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
items.hook: Don’t quit in the compound-interest zone.
items.lesson: Weariness often arrives right before the harvest. Keep the cadence.

items.text: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,
items.hook: Work as if the audience is bigger than the standup.
items.lesson: Craft for the real standard — not just the nearest manager.

items.text: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been exercised thereby.
items.hook: Discipline feels like loss until the fruit shows.
items.lesson: Training hurts in the moment; judgment shows later. Stay in the reps.

items.text: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
items.hook: Cast the anxiety — don’t hoard it.
items.lesson: Carrying every worry is a bad load balancer. Hand off what’s not yours.

items.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
items.lesson: The measure of love is what it gives away — not what it posts.

items.text: Go, and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
items.lesson: Go, teach, baptize — and remember the closer: you are not alone to the end.

items.text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
items.hook: Rest is an invitation, not a prize.
items.lesson: Bring the heavy load — don’t wait until you’ve earned the right to put it down.

items.text: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden. Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house. Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
items.lesson: Light on a stand serves the house. Hide it and everyone stumbles in the dark.

items.text: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.
items.hook: Way, truth, life — not a menu.
items.lesson: Some claims are exclusive on purpose. Decide whether you treat them as optional branding.

items.text: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
items.hook: Love God. Love neighbor. That’s the stack.
items.lesson: Two commandments collapse a thousand debates into a priority queue.

items.text: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
items.lesson: Before you ship the policy, ask how it feels from the other chair.

items.text: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
items.hook: Seek first — then the rest orders itself.
items.lesson: Priority is a filter. Wrong first things make every second thing feel scarce.

items.text: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
items.lesson: Passive wishing isn’t a strategy. Keep the loop open until the door moves.

items.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
items.hook: Love the ones who don’t love you back.
items.lesson: Enemy-love is the hard mode of neighbor-love — and the clearest tell of the real thing.

items.text: One of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together. Knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?” Jesus answered, “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment. The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
items.hook: The greatest command is not complicated.
items.lesson: One God, whole heart, neighbor as self — simple enough to memorize, hard enough to live.

items.text: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
items.hook: Pray for the people who hunt you.
items.lesson: Spite is easy energy. Prayer redirects it before it owns you.

items.text: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
items.hook: Heart, soul, strength, mind — all in.
items.lesson: Partial devotion is a split CPU. Whole-person love is the load.

items.text: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”
items.lesson: Discipleship gets recognized less by slogans than by how you treat each other.

items.text: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
items.lesson: Friendship’s ceiling isn’t affinity — it’s costly loyalty when it hurts.

items.text: If you love me, keep my commandments.
items.lesson: Affection without follow-through is theater. Keep the commands you claim to cherish.

items.text: From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”
items.lesson: Change direction before the map updates. Proximity to the good still demands a turn.

items.text: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
items.hook: Follow the treasure to find the heart.
items.lesson: Budgets and calendars confess what sermons won’t. Watch where attention settles.

items.text: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
items.lesson: Anxiety is expensive and sterile — it spends focus without extending life.

items.text: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
items.lesson: The standard you swing at others will return on you. Soften the gavel.

items.text: Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”
items.lesson: Before the body is healed, the deeper wound gets named: you are not stuck in guilt.

items.text: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
items.lesson: Human ceilings are real. Don’t confuse them with absolute ceilings.

items.text: He called the multitude to himself with his disciples, and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
items.hook: Take up the cross — then follow.
items.lesson: Discipleship isn’t a vibe. It’s costly alignment with a path you didn’t invent.

items.text: I and the Father are one.”
items.lesson: “I and the Father are one” is not teamwork talk — it’s a claim about who He is.

items.text: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
items.hook: Poverty of spirit is the doorway.
items.lesson: Kingdom entry starts with admitting you don’t have the leverage you pretend to.

items.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
items.lesson: Grief isn’t failure. It’s honesty about loss — and honesty is where comfort lands.

items.text: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
items.hook: The meek inherit — not the loudest.
items.lesson: Soft power outlasts domination theater. Strength under rein still wins the long game.

items.text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.
items.lesson: Appetite for justice is a feature. Starve it with cynicism and you get brittle.

items.text: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
items.lesson: What you withhold from others often becomes what you lack when you need it.

items.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
items.hook: Purity of heart clears the view.
items.lesson: Clouded motives make God and people look like mirrors of your agenda.

items.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
items.lesson: Peace isn’t passivity — it’s the hard craft of repairing what’s torn.

items.text: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
items.hook: Persecution for right still counts as blessing.
items.lesson: Pushback isn’t always a signal you’re wrong — sometimes it’s the cost of alignment.

items.text: But he said to them, “It is I. Don’t be afraid.”
items.hook: It is I — do not be afraid.
items.lesson: Presence collapses panic. Name who is in the boat before you name the storm.

items.text: Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. He who comes to me will not be hungry, and he who believes in me will never be thirsty.
items.hook: Bread that ends the hunger cycle.
items.lesson: Come and believe — the promise is satisfaction that scrolling never delivers.

items.text: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
items.hook: Follow the light or walk in dark.
items.lesson: Navigation needs a source. Pick a lamp brighter than your feed.

items.text: I said therefore to you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”
items.lesson: Some truths you can defer; this one claims your destination depends on trust.

items.text: Jesus therefore said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and I do nothing of myself, but as my Father taught me, I say these things.
items.lesson: Revelation arrives after the costly act — not before the risk feels safe.

items.text: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM. ”
items.lesson: This isn’t biography flex. It’s a claim that reorders history around a present tense.

items.text: I am the door. If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out, and will find pasture.
items.hook: The door that saves and pastures.
items.lesson: Entry and nourishment share one gate. Don’t invent a side entrance that starves you.

items.text: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
items.hook: The good shepherd spends his life.
items.lesson: Leadership that won’t bleed for the flock is hireling management.

items.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.
items.hook: Resurrection is a person, not a metaphor.
items.lesson: Belief rewrites death’s last word — even when the tomb still looks sealed.

items.text: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me, and I in him, the same bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
items.lesson: Branches don’t freestyle fruit. Stay connected or watch the yield collapse.

items.text: They answered him, “Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus said to them, “I am he.” Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.
items.hook: I am he — said in the arrest.
items.lesson: Identity doesn’t flinch when the cost arrives. He names himself in the trap.

items.text: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.
items.hook: Alpha and Omega — bookends of reality.
items.lesson: If He is first and last, mid-story panic loses its claim to be ultimate.

items.text: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.’”
items.hook: Bread alone is not a life.
items.lesson: Material supply without word leaves you fed and empty. Eat both.

items.text: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.
items.hook: Salt that loses savor is trash.
items.lesson: Distinctiveness is the job. Blend into the pile and you forfeit the point.

items.text: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
items.lesson: Shine so others credit the Source — not so you collect the spotlight.

items.text: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
items.lesson: If the feed is your reward, heaven has nothing left to pay.

items.text: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
items.lesson: Secret practice beats performative piety. The audience of One is enough.

items.text: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
items.lesson: Clenched fists can’t receive. Release the debt you keep rehearsing.

items.text: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
items.lesson: Split loyalty always picks a winner. Name which throne actually runs you.

items.text: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
items.hook: Life is more than the supply chain.
items.lesson: Food and clothes matter — anxiety about them shouldn’t become the whole plot.

items.text: He said to them, “Because of your unbelief. For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
items.lesson: Size of faith isn’t the metric — placement is. Tiny trust aimed right still relocates.

items.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.
items.hook: Save your life and lose it.
items.lesson: Clutching the self is the fastest way to forfeit it. Release to receive.

items.text: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?
items.hook: World gained, soul forfeit — bad trade.
items.lesson: Empire without a self left to enjoy it is a spreadsheet win and a human loss.

items.text: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.
items.lesson: Persistence isn’t nagging heaven — it’s refusing to treat silence as a final no.

items.text: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
items.lesson: Audit the fruit, not the costume. Soft branding is easy to fake.

items.text: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
items.hook: Fear the right scale of loss.
items.lesson: Body risk is real; soul risk is ultimate. Calibrate courage accordingly.

items.text: “Don’t think that I came to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.
items.lesson: Truth divides before it heals. Don’t confuse conflict with failure of the message.

items.text: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.
items.hook: Lose life for His sake — find it.
items.lesson: The path to keeping what matters is releasing what only feels like control.

items.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
items.lesson: Learn from the gentle Teacher. His load fits; ego’s load never does.

items.text: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.”
items.lesson: Speech and intent pollute faster than diet rules. Guard the mouth-exit.

items.text: and said, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn, and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
items.lesson: Status theater blocks entry. Humility is the ticket, not sophistication.

items.text: But Jesus said, “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”
items.lesson: Don’t gatekeep wonder. The kingdom already belongs to the unpretentious.

items.text: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
items.lesson: Wealth can thicken the ego until entry looks impossible. Hold riches loosely.

items.text: Jesus answered them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
items.hook: Watch — many will claim the name.
items.lesson: Deception often wears familiar branding. Test claims before you follow the crowd.

items.text: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
items.lesson: The window is open. Delay is a decision dressed as waiting.

items.text: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
items.lesson: He came for sinners, not the self-satisfied. Admit the need or miss the cure.

items.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
items.hook: Kingdom belongs to such as these.
items.lesson: Childlike receive-mode beats adult gatekeeping. Drop the barrier you built.

items.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
items.lesson: Hate for His sake is predicted. Endurance — not applause — is the finish line.

items.text: He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
items.hook: Not what I will — what You will.
items.lesson: Gethsemane honesty: want the cup gone, still choose the Father’s path.

items.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.
items.lesson: Open hands beat ledgered generosity. Don’t gift what you plan to reclaim in spite.

items.text: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
items.hook: Fire on the earth — already wishing it lit.
items.lesson: His mission isn’t mild maintenance. Expect disruption that purifies.

items.text: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
items.lesson: He came to enlarge life, not shrink it. Scarcity spirituality is a counterfeit.

items.text: “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
items.hook: Rejoice when you’re lied about for Him.
items.lesson: Insult for righteousness is odd fuel — treat it as confirmation, not catastrophe.

items.text: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
items.hook: Deny yourself, take the cross, follow.
items.lesson: Three verbs of discipleship: refuse ego, accept cost, keep moving after Him.

items.text: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.
items.hook: Don’t let your heart be troubled.
items.lesson: Trust is the anti-panic protocol. Believe God when the room starts shaking.

items.text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, give I to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
items.hook: Peace I leave — not as the world gives.
items.lesson: World-peace is a ceasefire. His peace holds when the ceasefire fails.

items.text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
items.hook: Not as I will, but as You will.
items.lesson: The hardest prayer surrenders the preferred outcome without pretending you don’t have one.

items.text: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.
items.lesson: Forgiveness from the cross redefines power — mercy while being wronged.

items.text: Yahweh your God will make you plenteous in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, for good; for Yahweh will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers; if you will obey Yahweh your God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which are written in this book of the law; if you turn to Yahweh your God with all your heart, and with all your soul.
items.lesson: As we devote our lives to serve God, He blesses the fruit of our labours with great delight and pleasure. Just as He rejoices to bless us, so also Christians should desire to serve Him. This unfathomable pleasure in serving is solely founded on the Word of God and living in accordance to it. When we follow His commands with all our heart, soul, and mind, God prospers our way over an abundance. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 3rd.

items.text: How precious is your loving kindness, God! The children of men take refuge under the shadow of your wings.
items.lesson: In the midst of the most desolate wilderness or most perilous storm, every child of Abraham may rejoice that the Lord offers Himself as the surest of shelters. Circumstance, no matter how treacherous, is of no great concern for the believer for he has an eternal and unshakable refuge, lacking of no good thing. By the blood of Christ, all the believer's sins are washed away and he need tremble no more at the wrath of the Almighty due him for the fall. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 4th.

items.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
items.lesson: God, through His love and grace, promises to forgive us every time we confess our sins to Him! He does not cut us off when we continually sin, but instead loves to lavish His unending grace on us. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 5th.

items.text: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
items.lesson: Even as we take on the identity of the One Whom we love, so will the world come to despise us even as it despised Him. He entered the world to save it, but was mocked, scorned, and afflicted. We ought to expect no less vile action from the world and its wicked corruption. Yet for Him Who overcomes and perseveres in the strength of His God-granted faith: life, eternal and abundant. Rejoice therefore in your suffering as it works for you a far more exceeding weight of glory! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 6th.

items.text: But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.” “Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?”
items.lesson: When we get to heaven, we will have an incorruptible and immortal body. Death will be conquered! My Prayer: O Lord, You sacrificed so much that I might live! Thank you for conquering death and allowing me to live with You forever. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 7th.

items.text: Blessed is the man who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to those who love him.
items.lesson: Find your strength in the Gospel promise. Overcome the slings and arrows of the enemy's wrought! Overcome them by the beautiful power of Christ. Trust your salvation to the sovereign hand of God. Persevere, O brothers and sisters, and you shall be welcomed with great fortune of riches! The crown of life shall be granted you and you shall glorify the Lamb! Love God for He first loved you! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 8th.

items.text: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
items.lesson: The Lord leads us in the paths of righteousness and sometimes those paths lead through the valley of the shadow of death. Though it is hard to walk through these valleys, we can praise Him because He leads us into the valley of the shadow of death and not the valley of death itself. Take heart that even in these tremulous times, the Lord's hand is mighty. And truly, we need fear no evil! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 9th.

items.text: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection;
items.lesson: By the power of the resurrection of Christ, we are freed from the horrible bondage of sin. Incredible! We are united with the Creator of both heaven and earth and transformed into His likeness of righteousness. Our sin was crucified with Christ Jesus and we now hold the remarkable privilege of being called His children. May our loving Father be glorified for His indescribable kindness and faithfulness. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 10th.

items.text: So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
items.lesson: Our Lord is mighty beyond imagining. His power and strength are above measure. None may stand against the weight of His arm. And He will protect us, His people, to everlasting. Having been made His children, we who believe live under His defence as long as there exist enemies to His throne. Rejoice in the fact of your salvation, O believer, for your redemption is to life eternal and unshakeable! The darts of the enemy may be of deadly flame, yet they shall never pierce His people! We rest under the banner of the King and sit in the shade of His mighty shield! Take heart in the strength of our Lord and give no fearful recognition to the weak boasting of the world's powers. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 11th.

items.text: Your faithfulness is to all generations. You have established the earth, and it remains.
items.lesson: God is the true measure of faithfulness. Never failing, His goodness endures forever. His salvation is eternal. His nature is unchanging. His glory is to everlasting. Depend upon the Lord Who is worthy! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 12th.

items.text: Peter said to them, “Repent, and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
items.lesson: Gifted with the very Spirit of God are we who have repented our sins and believed upon the risen Lord of the universe. Promised by Christ before He ascended to the heavenlies, the Holy Spirit will lead us in the paths of righteousness. Heed the Word of the Lord and proceed in every good work until the Son of heaven returns for His holy bride! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 13th.

items.text: You are of God, little children, and have overcome them; because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.
items.lesson: Though ever vigilant, the child of God need fear no false teacher or doctrine-he need fear no antichrist-for the power and grace and love and work of God have freed the believer from all fear. If God is for us, who then may stand against us? Truly, we have been crafted much more than conquerors in the strength of Christ Jesus! Believer, take hold of your identity! Give no sway to the doctrine of the flesh! Stand firm against the passions of men! Rejoice in your holy calling and irrevocable birthright! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 14th.

items.text: Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
items.lesson: Truly the child of faith should rejoice in His persecution for in it, he shall find union with Christ! O what beautiful, grim mystery that we, the church, should find our identity in the death of Christ-and by being found in His death we shall likewise be found in His resurrection! Rejoice! And live! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 15th.

items.text: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
items.lesson: God's grace is greater than our weakness. When we admit our weaknesses then more of Christ's strength can be manifested in us. We are used more when we are made less. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 16th.

items.text: I was angry because of the iniquity of his covetousness, and struck him; I hid myself and was angry; and he went on backsliding in the way of his heart. I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
items.lesson: Though the whole of mankind stands corrupted and damnable before the majesty of the Lord God Almighty, even so He promises to choose out for Himself a special people. Ever will He heal His dear children! In spite of their hearts of malice and stone, the Lord will be faithful to renew them and cause them to become the bearers of life eternal. Praise God that we who believe have received such mercy as this! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 17th.

items.text: As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.
items.lesson: Praise be to our ever-loving Father that He will always be faithful to chasten His children to correction. His discipline is of a caring love toward us-it is for our benefit, gracious and merciful. The Lord wants what is best for us and kindly prompts us to return to Him. Praise the Lord for His involvement. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 18th.

items.text: For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of partition,
items.lesson: The unity in Christ is far beyond that which men might craft. It is promised that all Abraham's seed, both Jew and Gentiles alike, are truly of one body-a body of faith! Love your brothers in Christ. Leap to aid each other even as Christ Himself leapt to save you-at His own peril. This is the Gospel. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 19th.

items.text: Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
items.lesson: Trust in the Lord, O son of righteousness, for He is worthy of your esteem. He is infinitely capable of caring for your needs and will always work even the most difficult of situations for benefit. Cast all your cares upon Him for He will be faithful to deliver you. Stand ever in your righteous hope in Christ and you shall not be moved. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 20th.

items.text: You also, as living stones, are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
items.lesson: O believers, take joy in the great honour bestowed upon you by the Lord Himself! Not only has He made you His son, pure and undefiled, but He has counted you worthy to be built together with your fellow saints and Christ Himself to be the very temple to house His Spirit. What a blessing it is to be the object of such a gift! Praise be to the Lord Almighty who has made us into living stones to take special and essential part in His sovereign plan! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 21st.

items.text: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
items.lesson: Jesus promised that He will always be with us, even to the end of the age. We as Christians have Christ as our authority and comfort. He is the Emmanuel (the God who came to earth to live with us) and though He has ascended to the Father, even so, He remains to live with us. Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 22nd.

items.text: In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.
items.lesson: Right now, Jesus is preparing a place for us in heaven! And someday He will come to take us to that place. How glorious will that day be when we behold with open face the beautiful majesty of our Lord! Open the full Blue Letter Bible reading for August 23rd.

items.text: He said to him, “Most certainly, I tell you, hereafter you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
items.lesson: Yes, to our faith this sight is plain even at this day. We do see Heaven opened. Jesus Himself has opened that kingdom to all believers. We gaze into the place of mystery and glory, for He has revealed it to us. We shall enter it soon, for He is the way. Now we see the explanation of Jacob's ladder. Between earth and Heaven there is a holy commerce; prayer ascends, and answers come down, by the way of Jesus, the M…

items.text: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
items.lesson: The last word in the Canticle of love is, "Make haste, my beloved," and among the last words of the Apocalypse we read, "The Spirit and the Bride say, Come"; to which the heavenly Bridegroom answers, "Surely I come quickly." Love longs for the glorious appearing of the Lord, and enjoys this sweet promise - "The coming of the Lord draweth nigh." This stays our minds as to the future. We look out with hope through t…

items.text: Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name. The upright will dwell in your presence.
items.lesson: Oh, that my heart may be upright, that I may always be able to bless the name of the Lord! He is so good to those that be good, that I would fain be among them, and feel myself full of thankfulness every day. Perhaps, for a moment, the righteous are staggered when their integrity results in severe trial; but assuredly the day shall come when they shall bless their God that they did not yield to evil suggestions an…

items.text: Yahweh looked at him, and said, “Go in this your might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Haven’t I sent you?”
items.lesson: What a look was that which the Lord gave to Gideon! He looked him out of his discouragements into a holy bravery. If our look to the Lord saves us, what will not His look at us do? Lord, look on me this day, and nerve me for its duties and conflicts. What a word was this which Jehovah spoke to Gideon! "Go." He must not hesitate. He might have answered, "What, go in all this weakness!" But the Lord put that word ou…

items.text: ‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great things, and difficult, which you don’t know.’
items.lesson: God encourages us to pray. They tell us that prayer is a pious exercise which has no influence except upon the mind engaged in it. We know better. Our experience gives the lie a thousand times over to this infidel assertion. Here Jehovah, the living God, distinctly promises to answer the prayer of His servant. Let us call upon Him again, and admit no doubt upon the question of His hearing us and answering us. He t…

items.text: Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish to you an everlasting covenant.
items.lesson: Notwithstanding our sins, the Lord is still faithful in His love to us. He looks back. See how He remembers those early days of ours when He took us into covenant with Himself, and we gave ourselves over to Him. Happy days those! The Lord does not twit us with them, and charge us with being insincere. No, He looks rather to His covenant with us than to our covenant with Him. There was no hypocrisy in that sacred c…

items.text: Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
items.lesson: Good old Jacob could no more be with Joseph, for his hour had come to die: but he left his son without anxiety, for he said with confidence, "God shall be with you." When our dearest relations, or our most helpful friends, are called home by death, we must console ourselves with the reflection that the Lord is not departed from us, but lives for us, and abides with us for ever. If God be with us, we are in ennobli…

items.text: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil; for he gives sleep to his loved ones.
items.lesson: Ours is not a life of anxious care, but of happy faith. Our heavenly Father will supply the wants of His own children, and He knoweth what we have need of before we ask Him. We may therefore go to our beds at the proper hour, and not wear ourselves out by sitting up late to plot, and plan, and contrive. If we have learned to rely upon our God we shall not lie awake with fear gnawing at our hearts; but we shall lea…

items.text: For this God is our God forever and ever. He will be our guide even to death.
items.lesson: We need a guide. Sometimes we would give all that we have to be told exactly what to do, and where to turn. We are willing to do right, but we do not know which out of two roads we are to follow. Oh, for a guide! The Lord our God condescends to serve us as guide. He knows the way, and will pilot us along it till we reach our journey's end in peace. Surely we do not desire more infallible direction. Let us place ou…

items.text: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.’”
items.lesson: If God so willed it we could live without bread, even as Jesus did for forty days; but we could not live without His Word. By that Word we were created, and by it alone can we be kept in being, for he sustaineth all things by the Word of His power. Bread is a second cause; the Lord Himself is the first source of our sustenance. He can work without the second cause as well as with it; and we must not tie Him down t…

items.text: But I will deliver you in that day,’ says Yahweh; ‘and you will not be given into the hand of the men of whom you are afraid.
items.lesson: When the Lord's faithful ones are suffering for Him, they shall have sweet messages of love from Himself, and sometimes they shall have glad tidings for those who sympathize with them and help them. Ebed-melech was only a despised Ethiopian, but he was kind to Jeremiah, and so the Lord sent him this special promise by the mouth of his prophet. Let us be ever mindful of God's persecuted servants, and He will reward…

items.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
items.lesson: Of all the stars in the sky the polestar is the most useful to the mariner. This text is a polestar, for it has guided more souls to salvation than any other Scripture. It is among promises what the Great Bear is among constellations. Several words in it shine with peculiar brilliance. Here we have God's love, with a "so" to it, which marks its measureless greatness. Then we have God's gift in all its freeness and…

items.text: Sing, heavens; and be joyful, earth; and break out into singing, mountains: for Yahweh has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
items.lesson: So sweet are the comforts of the Lord, that not only the saints themselves may sing of them, but even the Heavens and the earth may take up the song. It takes something to make a mountain sing; and yet the prophet summons quite a choir of them. Lebanon, and Sirion, and the high hills of Bashan and Moab, He would set them all singing because of Jehovah's grace to His own Zion. May we not also make mountains of diff…

items.text: Yahweh’s angel encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them.
items.lesson: We cannot see the angels, but it is enough that they can see us. There is one great Angel of the Covenant, whom not having seen we love, and His eye is always upon us both day and night. He has a host of holy ones under Him, and He causes these to be watchers over His saints and to guard them from all ill. If devils do us mischief, shining ones do us service. Note that the Lord of angels does not come and go, and…

items.text: My eyes will be on the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me. He who walks in a perfect way, he will serve me.
items.lesson: If David spoke thus, we may be sure that the Son of David will be of the same mind. Jesus looks out for faithful men, and He fixes His eyes upon them, to observe them, to bring them forward, to encourage them, and to reward them. Let no true-hearted man think that he is overlooked; the King Himself has His eye upon him. There are two results of this royal notice. First we read, "that they may dwell with me." Jesus…

items.text: You will arise and have mercy on Zion; for it is time to have pity on her. Yes, the set time has come. For your servants take pleasure in her stones, and have pity on her dust.
items.lesson: Yes, our prayers for the church will be heard. The set time is come. We love the prayer meeting, and the Sunday school, and all the services of the Lord's house. We are bound in heart to all the people of God, and can truly say, "There's not a lamb in all thy flock I would disdain to feed; There's not a foe before whose face I'd fear thy cause to plead." If this is the general feeling, we shall soon enjoy times of…

items.text: Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
items.lesson: Yes, Lord, we believe it; we shall never die. Our soul may be separated from our body, and this is death of a kind; but our soul shall never be separated from God, which is the true death - the death which was threatened to sin - the death penalty which is the worst that can happen. We believe this most assuredly, for who shall separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord? We are members of t…

items.text: the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment;
items.lesson: The godly are tempted and tried. That is not true faith which is never put to the test. But the godly are delivered out of their trials, and that not by chance, nor by secondary agencies, but by the Lord himself. He personally undertakes the office of delivering those who trust Him. God loves the godly or godlike, and He makes a point of knowing where they are, and how they fare. Sometimes their way seems to be a…

items.text: For I will surely save you, and you shall not fall by the sword, but your life shall be for a prey to you; because you have put your trust in me,’ says Yahweh.”
items.lesson: Behold the protecting power of trust in God. The great men of Jerusalem fell by the sword, but poor Ebed-melech was secure, for his confidence was in Jehovah. Where else should a man trust but in his Maker? We are foolish when we prefer the creature to the Creator. Oh, that we could in all things live by faith, then should we be delivered in all time of danger! No one ever did trust in the Lord in vain, and no one…

items.text: Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
items.lesson: It is a heavy burden, roll it on Omnipotence. It is thy burden now, and it crushes thee; but when the Lord takes it, He will make nothing of it. If thou art called still to bear it, "he will sustain thee." It will be on Him, and not on thee. Thou wilt be so upheld under it that the burden will be a blessing. Bring the Lord into the matter and thou wilt stand upright under that which in itself would bow thee down.…

items.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
items.lesson: By the valley of weeping we come to Zion. One would have thought mourning and being blessed were in opposition, but the infinitely wise Saviour puts them together, in this beatitude. What He has joined together let no man put asunder. Mourning for sin - our own sins, and the sins of others - is the Lord's seal set upon His faithful ones. When the Spirit of grace is poured upon the house of David, or any other hous…

items.text: Behold, at that time I will deal with all those who afflict you, and I will save those who are lame, and gather those who were driven away. I will give them praise and honor, whose shame has been in all the earth.
items.lesson: There are plenty of these lame ones, both male and female. You may meet "her that halteth" twenty times in an hour. They are in the right road, and exceedingly anxious to run in it with diligence, but they are lame, and make a sorry walk of it. On the heavenly road there are many cripples. It may be that they say in their hearts - What will become of us? Sin will overtake us, Satan will throw us down. Ready-to-hal…

items.text: Such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he pervert by flatteries; but the people who know their God shall be strong, and take action.
items.lesson: "The Lord is a man of war, Jehovah is his name." Those who enlist under His banner shall have a Commander who will train them for the conflict, and give them both vigor and valor. The times of which Daniel wrote were of the very worst kind, and then it was promised that the people of God would come out in their best colors: they would be strong and stout to confront the powerful adversary. Oh, that we may know our…

items.text: “Therefore behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.
items.lesson: The goodness of God sees us allured by sin, and it resolves to try upon us the more powerful allurements of love. Do we not remember when the Lover of our souls first cast a spell upon us and charmed us away from the fascinations of the world? He will do this again and again whenever He sees us likely to be ensnared by evil. He promises to draw us apart, for there He can best deal with us, and this separated place…

items.text: Your bars will be iron and brass. As your days, so your strength will be.
items.lesson: Here are two things provided for the pilgrim: shoes and strength. As for the shoes: they are very needful for traveling along rough ways, and for trampling upon deadly foes. We shall not go barefoot - this would not be suitable for princes of the blood royal. Our shoes shall not be at all of the common sort, for they shall have soles of durable metal, which will not wear out even if the journey be long and difficu…

items.text: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation.
items.lesson: This is our hope. He to whom we have already looked as coming once to bear the sins of many will have another manifestation to the sons of men; this is a happy prospect in itself. But that second appearing has certain peculiar marks which glorify it exceedingly. Our Lord will have ended the business of sin. He has so taken it away from His people, and so effectually borne its penalty, that He will have nothing to…

items.text: Those who are wise shall shine as the brightness of the expanse; and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars forever and ever.
items.lesson: Here is something to wake me up. This is worth living for. To be wise is a noble thing in itself: in this place it refers to a divine wisdom which only the Lord Himself can bestow. Oh to know myself, my God, my Saviour! May I be so divinely taught that I may carry into practice heavenly truth, and live in the light of it! Is my life a wise one? Am I seeking that which I ought to seek? Am I living as I shall wish I…

items.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahweh.
items.lesson: Betrothment unto the Lord! What an honor and a joy! My soul, is Jesus indeed thine by His own condescending betrothal? Then, mark, it is for ever. He will never break His engagement, much less sue out a divorce against a soul joined to Himself in marriage bonds. Three times the Lord says, "I will betroth thee." What words He heaps together to set forth the betrothal! Righteousness comes in to make the covenant leg…

items.text: “I will remember their sins and their iniquities no more.”
items.lesson: According to this gracious covenant the Lord treats His people as if they had never sinned. Practically, He forgets all their trespasses. Sins of all kinds He treats as if they had never been; as if they were quite erased from His memory. O miracle of grace! God here doth that which in certain aspects is impossible to Him. His mercy worketh miracles which far transcend all other miracles. Our God ignores our sin n…

items.text: He who overcomes will be arrayed in white garments, and I will in no way blot his name out of the book of life, and I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
items.lesson: Warrior of the cross, fight on! Never rest till thy victory is complete, for thine eternal reward will prove worthy of a life of warfare. See, here is perfect purity for thee! A few in Sardis kept their garments undefiled, and their recompense is to be spotless. Perfect holiness is the prize of our high calling, let us not miss it.

items.text: But go you your way until the end; for you shall rest, and shall stand in your lot, at the end of the days.
items.lesson: We cannot understand all the prophecies, but yet we regard them with pleasure, and not with dismay. There can be nothing in the Father's decree which should justly alarm His child. Though the abomination of desolation be set up, yet the true believer shall not be defiled; rather shall he be purified, and made white, and tried. Though the earth be burned up, no smell of fire shall come upon the chosen. Amid the cra…

items.text: It will be in that day,” says Yahweh, “that you will call me ‘my husband,’ and no longer call me ‘my master.’ For I will take away the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and they will no longer be mentioned by name.
items.lesson: That day has come. We view our God no more as Baal, our tyrant lord and mighty master, for we are not under law, but under grace. We now think of Jehovah, our God, as our Ishi, our beloved husband, our lord in love, our next-of-kin in bonds of sacred relationship. We do not reverence Him less, but we love Him more. We do not serve Him less obediently, but we serve Him for a higher and more endearing reason. We no…

items.text: “Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’
items.lesson: Nothing of man is sure; but everything of God is so. Especially are covenant mercies sure mercies, even as David said "an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure." We are sure that the Lord meant His mercy. He did not speak mere words: there is substance and truth in every one of His promises. His mercies are mercies indeed. Even if a promise seems as if it must drop through by reason of death, yet it…

items.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time;
items.lesson: This is tantamount to a promise: if we will bow down, the Lord will lift us up. Humility leads to honor: submission is the way to exaltation. That same hand of God which presses us down is waiting to raise us up when we are prepared to bear the blessing. We stoop to conquer. Many cringe before men, and yet miss the patronage they crave; but he that humbles himself under the hand of God shall not fail to be enriche…

items.text: Yahweh has taken away your judgments. He has thrown out your enemy. The King of Israel, Yahweh, is among you. You will not be afraid of evil any more.
items.lesson: What a casting out was that! Satan has lost his throne in our nature even as he lost his seat in Heaven. Our Lord Jesus has destroyed the enemy's reigning power over us. He may worry us, but he cannot claim us as his own. His bonds are no longer upon our spirits: the Son has made us free, and we are free indeed. Still is the arch-enemy the accuser of the brethren; but even from this position our Lord has driven hi…

items.text: Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
items.lesson: Surely He will come a second time, and then, when He sees us, and we see Him, there will be rejoicings indeed. Oh for that joyous return! But this promise is being daily fulfilled in another sense. Our gracious Lord has many "agains" in His dealings with us. He gave us pardon, and He sees us again, and repeats the absolving word as fresh sins cause us grief. He has revealed to us our acceptance before God, and whe…

items.text: Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”
items.lesson: Here is an urgent occasion - "the day of trouble." It is dark at noon on such a day, and every hour seems blacker than the one which came before it. Then is this promise in season: it is written for the cloudy day. Here is condescending advice, "call upon me."
